name: illustrator-save-as-foreignobject
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 28.6 - File > Save As... > SVG, "Preserve Illustrator Editing Capabilities" left ticked (the dialog default)
story: A student drew an ordinary two-line name plate and reached for Save As rather than Export As, so the artwork arrives inside Illustrator's private editing envelope.
idioms: an internal DTD subset declaring &ns_extend; &ns_ai; &ns_graphs; &ns_sfw; as entities, and the root then USING them as namespace URIs (xmlns:i="&ns_ai;")
<!DOCTYPE svg PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD SVG 1.1//EN" ...> ahead of the root element
the whole drawing inside <switch>, whose FIRST branch is <foreignObject requiredExtensions="&ns_ai;"> holding an <i:pgfRef> that points at the blob at the end of the file
the real artwork in the switch's second branch, marked <g i:extraneous="self">
a trailing <i:pgf id="adobe_illustrator_pgf"> holding the CDATA-wrapped, gzipped PGF copy of the document
width="1920px" height="1080px" WITH the px unit, beside viewBox and enable-background
x="0px" y="0px" on the root and xml:space="preserve"
PostScript face names in inner single quotes on a presentation attribute (font-family="'Archivo-Bold'"), font-size with a px unit, unitless letter-spacing
tab indentation, Illustrator's double space after a tag name (<sfw  xmlns=)
whyThisMatters: Save As is the command a non-technical person already knows, so this is the file shape a student produces by not reading the export guide - and docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md §6 only PREFERS Export As, it never says Save As is refused. Two things could go wrong and both are silent: the internal-DTD entities could make the document unparseable, in which case a perfectly ordinary drawing is refused with a message that names neither Save As nor the fix; and the <switch>/<foreignObject> envelope could take the artwork down with it when §8's sanitizer removes the foreignObject, since the drawing is the switch's SIBLING branch. It also pins the promise that a removal is reported rather than done quietly.
